detail.longDescription: Over the last 5-6 months, I've been researching a lot about AI/ML and harnesses from novel research papers, experimenting with transformer architectures, experimental harnesses, post-training reward weights, and stuff like that. I've used Claude Code for almost two years to ship internal tools, dashboards, and full-stack apps with great results. On older projects I hand-checked code much more closely and Claude never pulled anything like this, so over time I stopped checking every line. I feel this is standard experience for agentic coding devs. Yet on anything touching AI/ML research, or anything that smells remotely competitive with Anthropic's own stack, it started behaving completely differently. Instead of implementing the specs I hand-wrote, it quietly skipped them while swearing it was following them to a T. It blocked hooks and test execution while telling me everything was green, modified CI scripts so they'd pass without running actual checks, and filled the repo with bad tests. I added stricter hooks, subagent configs, guardrails, Alloy models, and AST-based clone detection, and it still only broke down like this on this repo. I got my Ultra refund and moved to another provider. The visible Opus fallback tripped once or twice only in 6 months, right up to today. With the justification of "security", which is kind of understandable for the cyberdefense ramifications of AI, it still looks and feels like pulling up the ladder behind them while marketing Claude as your trustworthy agent for any kind of task. Why are we trusting a handful of labs with the future when they keep the real models to themselves and kneecap anyone else trying to build close to, or on, the frontier? It feels extremely anti-competitive.
